source.title: HarmRLVR: Weaponizing Verifiable Rewards for Harmful LLM Alignment
source.authors: Yue-Yue Liu; Lijun Li; Xingjun Wang; Jing Shao

record.tranche_reason: It reports harmful SFT results and tests harmful-response behavior after a different harmful-training method, GRPO-based RLVR; it also evaluates a suffix-based jailbreak. These are conceptual tests rather than explicit replications of the original methods.
record.gate_note: The study tests harmful training using harmful prompt-response pairs (SFT) and harmful prompt-only RLVR, and reports a GCG adversarial-suffix result. It does not test benign instruction fine-tuning, response-position KL, compliant-prefix prefilling, decoding changes, safety localization in weights, or deepening safety training. PAIR, ReNeLLM, and CodeAttack results are recorded as related prompt-level attack results, not as tests of the specified suffix/prefix mechanism.
record.test_reason: The study trains safety-aligned 7–8B open models (Llama3, Llama3.1, Qwen2.5, Qwen3) on 64 harmful AIR-Bench prompts and measures harmful compliance (ASR, Harm) on HEx-PHI and AdvBench. It uses three methods: harmful SFT, which follows the Qi et al. configuration and is close to V1's original method; prompt-only GRPO (HarmRLVR), its main and different method; and DPO. It also reports a GCG suffix-attack ASR (V4) as a baseline. No benign fine-tuning, per-position KL, prefilling, localization or deepening experiment is run.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that GRPO with 64 response-free harmful prompts reverses safety alignment across five models (96.01% average ASR), outperforming harmful SFT, DPO and jailbreaks while preserving utility. They find that T-Vaccine and SafeLoRA weaken against it, and that reward-reversed SafeRLVR cannot repair attacked models. They read this as showing that alignment imposes only surface-level constraints.
record.recipe_differences: The central intervention is on-policy GRPO optimization against a harmfulness reward using harmful prompts without responses, rather than the original fine-tuning recipes. The paper includes harmful SFT as a baseline but does not claim to reproduce the original studies.
record.method_sensitivity: Results vary by training method (SFT versus RLVR), model, evaluation dataset, number of harmful prompts, and adapter setting (full fine-tuning versus LoRA).

fits_no_version.finding: PAIR, ReNeLLM and CodeAttack reach 18.7%, 70.0% and 46.0% ASR on Llama3.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Prompt-level black-box jailbreaks partially bypass refusal, with success depending on the method.

fits_no_version.finding: HarmRLVR reaches high harmfulness with low aggregate KL from the base model: 0.03 on harmful data versus 0.18 for SFT.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Harmful compliance can be induced with a small aggregate distribution shift.

fits_no_version.finding: On DeepSeek-R1-Distill, which is not safety-aligned, harmful training raises ASR from 24–34% to 80–99%.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Harmful training raises harmful completion in non-safety-aligned models.

fits_no_version.finding: Reward-reversed GRPO on HarmRLVR-attacked Llama3 barely lowers ASR (96.86 to 96.48) while utility collapses (7.73 to 2.73). The same method aligns unaligned DeepSeek-R1 (29.05 to 0.36).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Safety is hard to restore by re-alignment after reward-driven harmful training.

fits_no_version.finding: T-Vaccine and SafeLoRA reduce harmfulness less against HarmRLVR than against SFT. SafeLoRA threshold projection lowers Harm from 4.96 to 3.33.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Defenses against harmful fine-tuning are less effective against RL-based harmful training.

record.peer_reviewed: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
record.problems: The reported attack metrics do not include uncertainty intervals. Automatic harmfulness evaluation uses GPT-4o-mini; the human-validation sample is 50 outputs. Experiments are limited to open-source models, primarily 7B and 8B, as the authors note. The study does not measure response-position KL or test compliant-prefix prefilling or decoding changes.
record.rows_left_out: No relevant reported result rows were left out.

untested.parts: No sweep of example count under SFT (only 64 examples). No models beyond 7–8B open weights, and no closed or API fine-tuning.
All of it: no benign fine-tuning is measured. Mix-1000 is used only inside the T-Vaccine defense test.
All of it. Table 9 reports only aggregate KL, not per-position KL.
Compliant-prefix prefilling, decoding changes, and whether bypass depends on the first response tokens.
All of it. The LoRA comparison and the SafeLoRA defense do not test whether a small set of weights or ranks carries safety.
All of it. The 'surface level' remark is an interpretation, not a test of the data or objective causing shallowness.
All of it: no training that spreads safety beyond the first tokens is tested.

missing.what: Harmful DPO with 64 preference pairs on Llama3 reaches 42.41% ASR (partial for V1); the authors say outputs mostly repeat the prompt.
KL-setting ablation for HarmRLVR: no KL 96.86, KL in loss 94.07, KL in reward 87.21 ASR.
SFT learning-rate and epoch sweep on Llama3: 4 epochs gives 9% ASR; lr 5e-5 (Qi et al.) peaks at 72/83.46%.
Qwen3 CoT and reward ablation (69.71 / 84.04 / 91.51 ASR) and rollout ablation (84.04 vs 94.07).
Results on HarmBench and JailbreakBench: SFT 81.5/77.0, RLVR 97/97, base 2.0.
Refusal-keyword ASR at zero perturbation: base 2.5, SFT 57.5, RLVR 100.

record.verdict_notes: Neither original source is this study, so V1 verdicts are allowed. The SFT baseline follows Qi et al.'s configuration with a retuned learning rate, so the SFT rows approach T1 for V1; HarmRLVR makes the study T2 overall. The reader's V1 limits_scope label rested on SFT being weaker than RLVR and keeping disclaimers. That does not qualify V1, so it was replaced with adapter, hyperparameter and CoT conditions. The duplicate V4 supports/limits_scope pair on the single row r30 was collapsed into one limits_scope label. The 'surface level' language is an interpretation and does not test V3 or V6. All harmfulness scores come from GPT-4o-mini, checked against human ratings on 50 samples (kappa 0.825). No uncertainty intervals are reported.

versions.untested_parts: The SFT baseline uses 64 harmful prompt-response pairs; the study does not test the full range of few-to-hundreds examples under SFT. Its 10–314 prompt sweep is for RLVR, not SFT.
No ordinary or carefully selected benign instruction fine-tuning is tested for raising harmful compliance.
No per-token KL by response position or aligned-versus-base positional comparison is reported.
GCG provides a suffix-attack result. The study does not test compliant-opening prefills or decoding changes, and does not measure whether effects depend on the first few response tokens.
The full-fine-tuning versus LoRA comparison tests attack performance under parameter constraints, not whether a small set of weights or ranks carries safety behavior.
The study does not test whether data or a training objective produces first-token shallowness.
The reward-reversal safety realignment experiment does not test training that spreads safety beyond the first response tokens.
